label: Haircut

what_happens.title: What happens at a haircut
goals: The steps: salon door, big chair, cape, spray, comb, snip, mirror
Hair can't feel anything, so snipping is just a sound
It ends with a look in the mirror
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the steps in order and show the tools on your own hair first.

who_is_there.title: Who cuts my hair
goals: The hairdresser's job is to make hair neat and comfy
The grown-up stays close and can be seen in the mirror
who_is_there.parentSkill: Introduce the hairdresser by name and job before the chair.

what_i_do.title: What I do in the chair
goals: Sit still like a statue, look in the mirror, keep hands under the cape
Ask for a break by saying 'stop please'
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise 'statue still' for a count of ten with a towel cape.

if_scared.title: If it feels strange
goals: Spray can feel cold, a comb can tug, clippers buzz and tickle
Hair grows back, and it is okay to feel unsure
Calm tools: counting to ten, holding a toy, a hand to hold
if_scared.parentSkill: If your child gets upset, pause, breathe together, and offer a short break.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise a haircut
goals: Play salon at home with a towel cape, a spray bottle and a comb
Go through the steps once more, ending at the mirror
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child give a toy a pretend haircut first.

steps: Walk into the salon and say hello
Climb into the big chair, maybe on a booster seat
Put on a cape that covers the clothes
Spray a little water and comb the hair
Snip with scissors or buzz with clippers
Look in the mirror at the new haircut
sensory: little hairs that feel itchy on the neck
a comb that can tug a knot
honestyNotes: Cutting hair itself has no feeling, but a comb can tug, little hairs can itch, and the clippers buzz and tickle. Never promise 'it won't feel like anything'; describe each feeling honestly.

fallbackAnswer: Hair can't feel anything, so the snip is just a sound.
Sometimes the comb tugs a knot a little, and you can say ouch and the hairdresser goes slower.
Yes. Hair grows back all the time, a tiny bit every day.
That's why people get haircuts again and again.
The buzzy clippers can tickle, and little hairs can feel itchy.
It's okay to giggle, and the brush sweeps the itchy hairs away.
A hairdresser. Their job is to make hair neat and comfy.
They'll say hello and tell you what they're doing.
You can see [[GROWNUP]] in the big mirror the whole time.
First the big chair and the cape, then a spray of water and a comb.
Then snip, snip, and last, a look in the mirror.

questionButtons.text: Will water go in my eyes?
fallbackAnswer: The hairdresser sprays gently and can cover your eyes with a hand.
You can close your eyes during the spray, too.

questionButtons.text: Why is the hairdryer so loud?
fallbackAnswer: A hairdryer blows warm air, whoosh, and it makes a loud sound.
You can cover your ears, or ask for a towel instead of the hairdryer.
A little different, a bit neater.
You are still you, and your hair keeps growing.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during each part; the part is often done before ten.

techniques.label: Practising the cape at home
techniques.how: Wear a towel as a cape at home first, so the real cape feels familiar.

techniques.label: Sitting on a grown-up's lap
techniques.how: Ask if your child can sit on your lap, with a cape over you both.

techniques.label: Holding a favourite toy
techniques.how: Let your child hold a toy under the cape; the toy can get a pretend haircut first.

techniques.label: Feeling the buzz first
techniques.how: Ask the hairdresser to let your child feel the clippers buzz on a hand before the head.

techniques.label: Saying 'stop please'
techniques.how: Agree a short break signal and ask the hairdresser to honour it.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Covering ears for the loud parts
techniques.how: Let your child cover the ears or wear ear muffs for the clippers and the hairdryer.

techniques.label: Choosing the haircut together
techniques.how: Look at a picture together and let your child choose between two styles.

pain: Hair can't feel anything. The snip is just a sound.
If the comb tugs, say ouch and we'll go slower.
body: Hair grows back a tiny bit every day.
The hairdresser only touches your hair.
sensory: The clippers buzz and tickle. It's okay to giggle.
Little hairs can itch. We'll brush them away.
strangers: The hairdresser's job is to make hair neat. Let's say hello.
They'll tell you what they're doing each time.
separation: I'm right here. You can see me in the mirror.
Want to sit on my lap?
unknown: First the cape, then the spray, then snip, then the mirror.
Let's count to ten for each part.
safety: Hairdressers use scissors very carefully every day.
You can say 'stop please' and they'll wait.
social: Lots of people get haircuts. Look, someone else is in a chair too.
Your toy can watch and cheer you on.
love: I love your hair long or short.
